title: Waiting for perfect data—or assuming AI will repair the data for you
summary: Prepare the data needed for the chosen use case without making every project depend on a complete enterprise rebuild.
diagnosis: Two opposite assumptions create delay or failure: that all data must be cleaned before any experiment, or that a model can compensate for missing, stale and inaccessible information. Determine the minimum trustworthy input for the chosen scope. A read-only experiment may be possible before a major migration, but its source limits and the cost of adapting it later must remain visible. While pragmatic local extracts accelerate early validation, bolting AI onto locked transactional applications creates fragile integration plumbing. A sustainable architecture requires moving toward independent, governed data where business semantics travel bound to each object, demoting transactional systems from data gatekeepers to consistency engines.
diagnostic_questions: Which specific data defects prevent this use case from meeting its acceptance criteria?
Can the useful scope be narrowed while preserving permissions, freshness and a clear explanation of limitations?
What changes when the source system migrates, and who will maintain the adapter or replacement?
Does the extracted data carry its business semantics and governance rules with it, or will every downstream workflow have to re-engineer context?
proposed_actions: Create a use-case data contract naming required fields, definitions, coverage, freshness, access and known gaps.
Repair or constrain the blocking issues first; test representative extracts before authorising consequential actions.
Consider staged read-only access, a replica or an approved integration where appropriate, documenting lag, reconciliation and migration dependencies rather than assuming them away.
working_artifact: Use-case data readiness record: required sources and fields; permitted purpose; definitions; completeness; freshness target; owner; access path; known exclusions; remediation; future migration impact.
measures: Task failure and escalation attributable to missing, stale, inconsistent or inaccessible data.
Share of required fields meeting the declared contract for the actual eligible population.
Time to a bounded trustworthy experiment, plus the maintenance and adaptation cost it creates.
tradeoff: The supplied materials do not demonstrate that a replica or pre-migration route is feasible in any particular ERP environment. That is an architecture option to assess locally. Maintain the tension between speed and independence: local extracts enable rapid learning today, but accumulating unmanaged ad-hoc extracts recreates the architectural lock-in they bypassed. Avoid replacing a justified data programme with a collection of fragile AI-specific pipelines.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: a purchasing team tests a read-only answer service on a defined set of approved supplier records, rather than waiting for the entire ERP migration or pretending the extract includes every supplier.
